note: The single source of truth for the read gateway's deployed configuration.
wrangler.toml is GENERATED from this file by ops/render-environments.py. Edit this file,
re-render, and commit both. The deploy gate refuses to deploy if the committed wrangler.toml
does not match what this file renders to, so an environment cannot drift from its record.
Nothing secret belongs in this file. The three secrets of every environment - the signing
keys, the operator token and the repository credential - are set per environment with
'wrangler secret put --env <env>' and are listed here only by name, so that the gate can
check that each environment has its own.
The three environments are separated in three ways, and the gate checks all three:
- by worker name: they are different Workers, with different Durable Object namespaces;
- by key id: the sets of key ids are disjoint, so a link minted for one environment is
- by secrets: each environment holds its own values, which the operator sets separately.
ceiling_notes: MAX_TTL may not exceed 259200 (72 h) and CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE may not exceed 120 seconds.
These are the operator's approved ceilings (docs/decisions/0003) and the gateway refuses to
start with a larger value. The renderer refuses to write a configuration that breaks them.

test.label: the local test environment: CI, the conformance suite and the operator's laptop

staging.label: staging: a disposable deployment used for the pilot and for operational rehearsal
notes: Staging reads a DISPOSABLE source. It must never be pointed at the repository that
staging is meant to rehearse against by accident, and its keys are not the production keys.
Staging is the environment where the pilot (Stage 6) runs, so it must be able to reach a
disposable copy of the source content.
The disposable source is the branch 'staging/source' of the repository below, seeded by
ops/staging-estate.py. The commit the pilot pins is the head of that branch; a capability
always pins a commit, so a moving branch never reaches the source adapter.
The fixture holds one file inside each allowed prefix and one file outside them
(plans/PILOT-001/private/notes.md), which is the negative case for Stage 6.2.4.
The staging key id is 's1' and is disjoint from production's, so a staging-minted link
cannot be replayed against production even if the two environments shared a worker name.

production.label: production: the gateway the operator's own tasks are served by
notes: The host is part of the work-order contract: docs/decisions/0002 requires the host to be
one the Class B agent's proxy is allowed to contact. It is not a free choice.
Production has no workers.dev exposure. The gateway is reachable on one named host only.
The key id is 'p1' and is disjoint from staging's, so a staging-minted link cannot be
replayed against production even if the two environments shared a worker name.
